drivingQuestion: From where is it derived that offering up outside items that are eaten, not burned, is exempt?
outcomeNote: the baraita's answer follows in zevachim.sugya432

segments.he: הַמַּעֲלֶה מִבְּשַׂר חַטָּאת [וְכוּ׳]. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן לַמַּעֲלֶה מִבְּשַׂר חַטָּאת, וּמִבְּשַׂר אָשָׁם, וּמִבְּשַׂר קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים, וּמִבְּשַׂר קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, וּמִמּוֹתַר הָעוֹמֶר, וּשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם, וְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים, וּשְׁיָרֵי מְנָחוֹת – שֶׁפָּטוּר?
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «One who offers up» outside the Temple courtyard a portion «of the meat of a sin offering» that is eaten, or who offers up a portion of several other items, is exempt. With regard to the reasoning behind this halakha, «the Sages taught» in a baraita: «From where» is it derived «that one who offers up» outside the Temple courtyard a portion «of the meat of a sin offering, or» a portion «of the meat of a guilt offering, or» a portion «of the meat of offerings of the most sacred order, or» a portion «of the meat of offerings of lesser sanctity, or» a portion «of the surplus of the omer offering, or the two loaves, or the shewbread, or the remainder of meal offerings» is «exempt,» as all these are eaten by the priests and not sacrificed on the altar?
